key_insight: PatientAgentBench shows that patient-facing health AI agents still make meaningful safety and workflow mistakes when tested in realistic, tool-using conversations.
clinical_relevance: For primary care and triage workflows, the study suggests agentic systems need stricter evaluation than static Q&A benchmarks before they can be trusted with patient-facing tasks.
method: Benchmarked 10 models across 4 model families on 1,200 simulated patient scenarios
Wrapped foundation models in an agent with healthcare tools and a simulated patient conversation
Used an LLM-as-a-Jury scoring system across 6 clinician-grounded dimensions, then validated against licensed clinician ratings
evidence_signal: The authors report 79-93% adjacent agreement between the jury and clinician raters, and model performance ranged from 32% to 88% on triage quality, with the strongest overall score only 4.25/5.
watch_item: Even strong models still failed on unverified tool outputs, missing crisis resources, and unsafe action-taking, so real-world deployment would need careful guardrails and human oversight.
paper_title: PatientAgentBench: A Benchmark Framework for Evaluating Patient-Facing Health AI Agents
